Decision (findings: root per-call context reached 365k-747k tokens and root cache reads dominate its cost): cap the root's context. Ship an autocompact threshold well below the default for the root (about 200k tokens) through the settings HolyAgent controls, if Claude Code supports one, and keep the root rule that reconcile restores state after compaction.

Decision: the root reads only what a decision needs. It accepts rendered work on Reviewer.visual's recorded evidence and reads an image only to show it to the user or to settle a concrete doubt; it runs no gates, data checks or probes itself (Worker.validation runs them).

Decision (finding: every brief crossed the root three times: create input, dispatch output, script text): assignment dispatch stores the brief as a file the specialist reads and prints a short prompt that points to it, so the root never sees or re-emits the brief after writing it; workflow scripts return only a short line per Assignment and the root closes each Assignment by piping the stored report to assignment close, reading only what judging needs.

Decision (finding: report evidence lines like 'Root effort: ...' did not match long criteria): assignment close matches an evidence line against a criterion's label, the text before the criterion's first colon, as well as its full text.

Decision (finding: status listed 87 unaccepted Assignments of old Intents into the root context): status and the SessionStart status show the unaccepted Assignments of the Intent in use and only a count for the others.
Decision (finding: the SessionStart context repeats the takeover line three times and restates rules the root prompt has): each rule and the takeover line reach the root once per session start.

Decision (findings: haiku thinking was 76-91% of its output, Sonnet integration ran merge-conflict and gate work at high effort, mechanical repairs went to Sonnet implementation): set Worker.operations, Worker.validation and Worker.mechanical to haiku medium and Worker.integration to sonnet medium; keep reviewers, implementation, debugging and visual at their current effort; the root's routing text names concrete haiku cases (data or list corrections, count fixes, conflict resolution in tests or generated files, gate runs, builds, screenshot capture).

Decision (findings: status-echo turns, ReadNotifications polls, sleep loops and scheduled re-checks while work ran): the root never polls notifications, schedules check-ins or runs wait loops while specialists or CI run; Monitor on gh pr checks --watch is the only CI wait, and a wake that changes nothing gets one short line.

Decision: the root's effort is high: the generated root agent declares effort high, and the settings HolyAgent recommends set the session effort to high where Claude Code supports it, so a main thread that is not the holyagent agent runs high too.
